title: Types of substances and bonds - 123 school
heading: Types of substances and bonds
intro: In chemistry you distinguish three kinds of substances, each with its own structure and its own typical bond. Metals consist of metal atoms: positive metal ions with free electrons between them (metallic bond). Salts consist of positive and negative ions (ionic bond). Molecular substances consist of uncharged molecules, which attract each other through the van der Waals bond (and through hydrogen bonds with -OH or -NH).
Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: Which three kinds of substances do you distinguish by the particles they are made of?
questions.a: Metals, salts and molecular substances

questions.q: Which particles make up a metal, a salt and a molecular substance?
questions.a: Metal: metal atoms (positive metal ions with free electrons). Salt: positive and negative ions. Molecular substance: uncharged molecules

questions.q: Which typical bond goes with metals, with salts and with molecular substances (between the molecules)?
questions.a: Metals: metallic bond. Salts: ionic bond. Molecular substances: van der Waals bond (and hydrogen bonds with -OH or -NH)

questions.q: How can you tell from the formula which kind of substance it is?
questions.a: Only a metal: metal. A metal with a non-metal: salt. Only non-metals: molecular substance
questions.e: Exception: a salt with the ammonium ion (NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup>) contains no metal but is still a salt.

questions.q: To which kind of substance does each of these formulas belong: Cu, KBr, CH<sub>4</sub> and (NH<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>?
questions.a: Cu: metal. KBr: salt. CH<sub>4</sub>: molecular substance. (NH<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>: salt
questions.e: Ammonium (NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup>) and sulfate (SO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup>) are ions, so there are no molecules and it is a salt.

questions.q: To which kind of substance does each of these formulas belong: Zn, CO<sub>2</sub>, Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> and C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>?
questions.a: Zn: metal. CO<sub>2</sub>: molecular substance. Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>: salt (iron(III) oxide). C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>: molecular substance (glucose)

questions.q: Is strontium (Sr) a metal or a non-metal? (use BINAS table 99)
questions.a: A metal
questions.e: Sr is in group 2 (the alkaline earth metals), on the left of the periodic table.

questions.q: What holds the particles in a metal together? Explain.
questions.a: The metallic bond: the attraction between the positive metal ions and the freely moving electrons between them

questions.q: What is a metal lattice?
questions.a: A regular arrangement of positive metal ions with the free electrons moving between them
questions.e: The valence electrons no longer belong to one atom but move through the whole lattice.

questions.q: Why does a metal conduct electric current even in the solid state?
questions.a: The free electrons can move through the lattice and carry charge with them

questions.q: Why do metals conduct heat well?
questions.a: The free electrons move quickly and carry kinetic energy from the hot part to the cold part

questions.q: Why can you bend or forge a metal without it breaking?
questions.a: The layers of metal ions can slide past each other; the free electrons keep the ions together, so the bond stays intact

questions.q: Name three properties that are typical for metals
questions.a: For example: conduct electricity, conduct heat, malleable, shiny, usually a high melting point
questions.e: If you got two of the three right, it counts as correct.

questions.q: What is an alloy? Give an example.
questions.a: A mixture of a metal with other elements (often other metals), for example bronze (copper and tin) or brass (copper and zinc)
questions.e: Steel (iron with a little carbon) is also an alloy.

questions.q: What happens to the electrons when a sodium atom and a chlorine atom form an ionic bond?
questions.a: Sodium gives one electron to chlorine: Na<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup> are formed
questions.e: Both ions now have a full outer shell (noble gas configuration).

questions.q: What is the difference between an ionic bond and an atomic (covalent) bond?
questions.a: Ionic bond: electrons are transferred and the ions attract each other. Covalent bond: atoms share electrons

questions.q: What is an ion lattice?
questions.a: A regular arrangement of positive and negative ions, in which each ion is surrounded by ions of the opposite charge

questions.q: A salt is made of charged ions. Why is a piece of salt neutral as a whole?
questions.a: The total positive charge is equal to the total negative charge

questions.q: Why do you call the formula of a salt a ratio formula and not a molecular formula?
questions.a: A salt does not consist of molecules. The formula only gives the smallest ratio in which the ions occur
questions.e: So NaCl means: as many Na<sup>+</sup> ions as Cl<sup>-</sup> ions, not a separate NaCl molecule.

questions.q: Why is a salt crystal brittle and does it break if you hit it hard?
questions.a: A shift puts ions with the same charge next to each other; they repel each other and the crystal splits

questions.q: Water melts at 0 °C, table salt only at about 800 °C. Explain this difference.
questions.a: In table salt the ions attract each other strongly (ionic bond), in ice the bonds between the molecules are weak. Melting salt takes much more energy

questions.q: Magnesium oxide (Mg<sup>2+</sup> and O<sup>2-</sup>) melts at about 2850 °C, sodium chloride (Na<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup>) at about 800 °C. Explain this difference.
questions.a: The ions in magnesium oxide have a larger charge (2+ and 2-), so the attraction is stronger and more energy is needed to melt it

questions.q: What happens to the ion lattice when a salt dissolves in water?
questions.a: The water molecules pull the ions out of the lattice and surround them; the ions move freely in the water

questions.q: Which two kinds of bond are there in liquid water and where are they?
questions.a: Covalent bonds inside the H<sub>2</sub>O molecules (strong) and hydrogen bonds between the molecules (weaker)

questions.q: Why do molecular substances usually have a low melting and boiling point?
questions.a: When melting and boiling only the weak bonds between the molecules are broken, not the covalent bonds inside the molecules

questions.q: A substance conducts electric current in the solid state. Which kind of substance is it?
questions.a: A metal
questions.e: Of the three kinds of substances only metals conduct current in the solid state, because of the free electrons.

questions.q: A substance does not conduct current in the solid state, but does when melted. Which kind of substance is it?
questions.a: A salt
questions.e: In the melt the ions can move freely.

questions.q: A substance conducts current neither as a solid nor as a liquid. Which kind of substance is it usually?
questions.a: A molecular substance
questions.e: There are no free electrons or ions.

questions.q: A metal and a molten salt both conduct current. What is the difference in the particles that carry the charge?
questions.a: In a metal free electrons carry the charge, in a molten salt the moving ions do

questions.q: You dissolve sugar in water and you dissolve table salt in water. Which solution conducts current and why?
questions.a: The table salt solution, because it contains free ions. Sugar stays in the water as molecules
